reviews.title: 3 TAALI /CLAP GARBA TUTORIAL | LEARN BASIC GARBA FOR BEGGINERS
reviews.countInterpretation: unverified; do not infer that the title counts beats or identifies one canonical Tran Taali sequence

visualObservations: Solo footwork demonstration shows short forward and forward/crossed placements, lateral/profile travel and return to front-facing or feet-apart pauses; the instructor repeatedly looks down to indicate the feet.

At sampled moments one leg lifts or reaches low forward/outward while the other supports a wide stance. Arms alternate between held behind/near the waist and brief gathered positions near the abdomen/chest.
The frames do not establish a complete cycle or exact step-side order; hand positions during the isolated footwork cannot be assumed to represent the later three-taali clap pattern.
unknowns: whether a full cycle is shown
whether and when any clap is integrated with this footwork

visualObservations: The instructor mostly stands in place with feet close or apart while demonstrating hand shapes: forearms cross at the chest, hands gather/clasp at chest height, palms meet at the sternum or to one side, then both hands extend forward together and lower toward the feet.
Several sampled palm-together shapes are held for explanation; still frames and unavailable captions/audio cues do not establish audible clap contacts or a three-clap sequence.
Near 4:54–5:10 the instructor bends toward the floor/foot area and gestures low, then returns to hands-forward and side-facing positions.
unknowns: actual clap count and contact sounds
footwork while each arm shape is shown
whether the hand lesson demonstrates a continuous dance phrase or separate positions

visualObservations: The instructor resumes a more mobile phrase with forward/diagonal travel and hands gathered or extended in front.

A high knee lift is shown with both arms rising overhead; later the instructor drops into a low bent-knee reach with the arms moving down/back, then returns to another knee-lift shape with the forearms crossed near the chest.
This demonstrates contrasting high and low body levels and arm positions, but the sparse samples do not prove that these are one continuous pattern or show clap contact.
unknowns: support foot and step-to-step landing order
whether the raised knee alternates sides

visualObservations: The instructor is in a close direct-to-camera explanation with hands clasping/opening near the abdomen; the video reaches its end card at the end of the 6:47 runtime.
unknowns: whether any last verbal cue labels a movement; captions are unavailable

provisionalTeacherCues.transcriptCue: The auto-generated Hindi transcript renders '12' near 1:12 and '34' near 1:17 during the solo passage. These may be count fragments, but the caption wording, spoken count sequence and alignment to musical beats are unconfirmed.
Auto-transcript renders 'this is our right one'; context and intended meaning are unclear.

visualObservations: In the solo movement passage, the demonstrator travels across the stage with his hands held behind his torso, then pauses in front-, profile- and back-facing wide or narrow stances.

Sampled lower-body actions include a forward placement, a low forward/side leg extension, a lifted-leg shape and a wide sideward reach/weight shift; sparse frames do not reveal every landing or whether these are separate named units.

The arms stay behind the torso through most of this solo passage, so no synchronized clap or matching hand pattern is visible. The solo passage ends and the pair is back in a stationary teaching pose by about 110 seconds.
unknowns: whether leg lifts/extensions are distinct named units
whether the arm-behind pose is a teaching simplification

visualObservations: Teaching pose with a bent hand near the head transitions into a wider stance, forward arm sweep, and contrasting high/low arm lines; exact foot contacts are unclear.
The pair pivots and travels around one another, alternating an overhead arm with a low or outward-reaching arm.
A later phrase brings the pair back into a wide stance with arms opened high/outward, then the woman turns with her skirt flaring while the man follows or marks beside her.
unknowns: exact sequence order between sampled frames

visualObservations: At about 197 seconds a cross-step toward the camera is sampled with the arms low/outward; the exact crossing foot is unclear.

From about 205–212 seconds, the pair cycles through a passing/traveling phrase: one dancer turns while the other opens or bends one arm high and keeps the other low/outward; both change between front, profile and back orientations. The woman's skirt flares during her pivots, partly hiding foot contacts.

From about 216–220 seconds the pair continues exchanging position and facing with broad high/low arm sweeps; a reach toward the partner is visible, but contact is not confirmed. A later turn with a broad raised/outward arm sweep is sampled near 225 seconds.

Around 232 and 245 seconds, the dancers continue turning with contrasting overhead and low/outward arms; the woman pivots with her skirt flaring while the man marks or travels beside her. Around 251 seconds they face more toward the camera and advance/turn into a close foreground position. The dance demonstration ends and the channel end card begins by about 257 seconds.
unknowns: continuous step order and landing sequence
turn direction relative to the partner/circle
whether either reach includes partner contact
